content: The studies listed were excluded for various reasons, primarily due to their failure to examine the effects of continued breastfeeding. 1. Mortenson (2002): This study categorized subjects into five groups based on breastfeeding duration but did not investigate the effects of continued breastfeeding. The groups were: ≤1 month, 2–3 months, 4–6 months, 7–9 months, and >9 months. 2. Muino (2008): Excluded because it did not study continued breastfeeding. Breastfeeding durations of 9 months and <1 month were mentioned. 3. Naz (2016): This study analyzed lactation duration as a continuous variable and its effect on osteoporosis but did not address continued breastfeeding. 4. Negri (1996): Excluded as it was a hospital-based case-control study. 5. Newcomb (1994, 1999): Both studies were case-control studies, with cases selected from statewide tumor registries, and did not focus on continued breastfeeding. 6. Nianogo (2017): Investigated the effects of exclusive breastfeeding for more or less than 6 months on childhood adiposity but did not study continued breastfeeding. 7. Niegel (2008): Excluded for not studying continued breastfeeding. 8. Nikpour (2012): A hospital-based case-control study that did not examine continued breastfeeding. 9. Nurmukhamedova (2015): Subjects were divided based on total breastfeeding duration (0, 1–48, 49–96, and ≥97 months), but continued breastfeeding (12–24 months) was not studied. 10. Nzefa (2019): Focused on ongoing breastfeeding in older children as a factor for undernutrition but did not study continued breastfeeding. 11. Oddy (2002, 2002a, 2004, 2004a, 2006, 2011, 2011a): These studies measured early infant feeding and breastfeeding duration but did not analyze continued breastfeeding. Breastfeeding durations were categorized variably, such as <4 months, 4–6 months, and >6 months. 12. Oh (2017): A case-only analysis that did not study continued breastfeeding. 13. Ohlendorf (2019): Excluded for not studying continued breastfeeding. The mean breastfeeding duration was 5 weeks (range: 0–40 weeks). 14. Oken (2008, 2013): Analyzed breastfeeding duration without distinguishing between exclusive and supplemented breastfeeding but did not study continued breastfeeding. 15. Onyango (1999, 2000): Did not provide data on continued versus short breastfeeding durations. Breastfeeding was classified as short, medium, or long based on the percentage of the study period. 16. Oran (2004): A hospital-based case-control study that did not examine continued breastfeeding. 17. Ortega-Garcia (2018): Studied the effect of breastfeeding duration on obesity but did not analyze continued breastfeeding. 18. Owen (1993): Presented data only on feeding during the first six months and did not study continued breastfeeding. 19. Pajuelo-Ramirez (2011): Investigated the effect of breastfeeding on obesity but did not study continued breastfeeding. 20. Panpanich (2003): Compared exclusively breastfed children with partially and non-breastfed children but did not study continued breastfeeding. 21. Park (2018): Examined breastfeeding durations of 0–17 months, 18–35 months, 36–52 months, 54–92 months, and 96–324 months but did not study continued breastfeeding across 12–24 months. 22. Pasricha (2011): Excluded due to the absence of a control group. 23. Paton (2003): Compared women who breastfed >1 month with those who never breastfed but did not study continued breastfeeding. 24. Pattison (2019): Analyzed the effects of never breastfeeding, breastfeeding for 0–6 months, and <6 months on illnesses and obesity but did not study continued breastfeeding. 25. Perera (2014): Reported the effects of breastfeeding for >2 years versus <2 years but did not study continued breastfeeding. 26. Perez (2013): Examined breastfeeding durations of no breastfeeding, <1 month, 1–3 months, 3–6 months, and 6–12 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 27. Peters (2013): Divided breastfeeding duration into six categories but did not study continued breastfeeding. 28. Pirila (2014): Studied breastfeeding duration as a continuous variable using logistic regression but did not analyze continued breastfeeding. 29. Portela (2015): Stratified the sample by breastfeeding duration and performed descriptive analysis but did not study continued breastfeeding. 30. Purvis (2005): Analyzed breastfeeding durations of never, <6 months, and >6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 31. Quigley (2018): Excluded for not studying continued breastfeeding. 32. Ram (2008): Used logistic regression to study the effect of lactation duration on metabolic syndrome but did not study continued breastfeeding. 33. Ramon (1996): A hospital-based case-control study that did not examine continued breastfeeding. 34. Rapp (2005): Analyzed exclusive breastfeeding durations of <2 months, 2–4 months, 4–6 months, and >6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 35. Rathnayake (2013): A school-based case-control study that was not representative and did not study continued breastfeeding. 36. Richards (2002): Classified breastfeeding duration as never, up to 2 months, 2–7 months, or >7 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 37. Ridd (2013): A conference abstract with no data on lactation durations. 38. Riman (2001, 2002): Institution-based case-control studies that did not study continued breastfeeding. 39. Rojano-Mejia (2011): Examined breastfeeding durations of 24 months, 36 months, and beyond but did not study continued breastfeeding. 40. Romieu (1996, 2000, 2018): Case-control studies with cases selected from hospitals, not representative of the population, and did not study continued breastfeeding. 41. Rosenbauer (2007, 2008): Case-control studies that did not study continued breastfeeding. 42. Rosenblatt (1995, 2004): Multinational hospital-based case-control studies that did not study continued breastfeeding. 43. Rothenbacher (2002, 2005): Analyzed breastfeeding durations of never, 0–3 months, 3–6 months, and ≥6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 44. Rust (2001): Excluded for not studying continued breastfeeding. 45. Ruuska (1992): Examined lactation durations of <6 months and ≥6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 46. Saarinen (1982): Divided subjects into three feeding groups but did not study continued breastfeeding. 47. Sadauskaitė-Kuehne (2004): A hospital-based case-control study that did not examine continued breastfeeding. 48. Saddlemire (2006): A hospital-based case-control study that did not study continued breastfeeding. 49. Sajjad (2015): Studied breastfeeding duration up to 10 months and beyond but did not study continued breastfeeding. 50. Sangaramoorthy (2019): A pooled analysis case-control study that did not study continued breastfeeding. 51. Sayegh (2005): Examined breastfeeding durations of 0, 0–18 months, and >18 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 52. Schack-Nielsen (2004, 2004a, 2006): Analyzed breastfeeding durations as continuous variables but did not study continued breastfeeding. 53. Scholtens (2008): Excluded for not studying continued breastfeeding. 54. Schuz (2001): Analyzed breastfeeding durations of <1 month, 1–6 months, and >6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 55. Sears (2002): Studied breastfeeding duration up to 26 weeks but did not study continued breastfeeding. 56. Shahidullah (1994): Did not assess the effects of continued versus shorter breastfeeding durations. 57. Sharma (2017): Studied the effect of exclusive breastfeeding duration on asthma but did not study continued breastfeeding. 58. Shehadeh (2006): Studied breast milk composition, not continued breastfeeding. 59. Shema (2007): A hospital-based case-control study that did not study continued breastfeeding. 60. Sherwood (2019): Analyzed breastfeeding duration as a continuous variable and its association with BMI but did not study continued breastfeeding. 61. Shields (2006): Categorized breastfeeding duration but did not study continued breastfeeding. 62. Shilbayeh (2003): Analyzed breastfeeding durations of 0–<1 month, 1–6 months, and >6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 63. Shu (1995, 1995a, 1999): Case-control studies that did not study continued breastfeeding. 64. Siltanen (2003): Reported on exclusive breastfeeding for >3 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 65. Silva (2006): Analyzed breastfeeding durations of never, <1 month, >1 and <3 months, and >3 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 66. Silvers (2012): Analyzed breastfeeding duration as a continuous variable but did not study continued breastfeeding. 67. Simondon (2001): Excluded for not studying continued breastfeeding. 68. Sipila (1988): Analyzed lactation durations of 1–6 months, 7–9 months, and ≥10 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 69. Siskind (1989): A case-control study with cases identified from hospitals that did not study continued breastfeeding. 70. Siti-Noor (2006): Defined prolonged breastfeeding as >6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 71. Skau (2019): Excluded due to the absence of a control group. 72. Smulevich (1999): A hospital-based case-control study that did not study continued breastfeeding. 73. Snijders (2007): Categorized breastfeeding duration but did not study continued breastfeeding. 74. Soke (2019): A case-control study with autism cases selected from specialized clinics, not representative of the population, and did not study continued breastfeeding. 75. Sonnenschein-van der Voort (2012): Categorized breastfeeding duration into four groups but did not study continued breastfeeding. 76. Soto-Ramirez (2012): Analyzed breastfeeding durations of <2 months, 2–3 months, and >4 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 77. Starodubova (2011): Examined breastfeeding durations of less and more than 6 months but did not study continued breastfeeding. 78. Strom (2018): Analyzed breastfeeding durations of ≥10 months and lesser but did not study continued breastfeeding. 79. Stuebe (2011): Studied maternal adipokines, not continued breastfeeding. 80. Stuver (1997): A hospital-based case-control study that did not study continued breastfeeding. 81. Su (2013): A hospital-based case-control study that was not population-representative and did not study continued breastfeeding. 82. Taylor (1984): Excluded for not studying continued breastfeeding.
